standing_rules.public_language: All PUBLIC artifacts (CHANGELOG entries, commit messages, release notes, README, PR descriptions) use terse user-visible language. NO mention of OpenClaw, Hermes, competitor names, strategy, capability matrices, monetization plans. Plans and rationale stay on Tony's ~/Desktop only.
standing_rules.local_only_deploys: Per CLAUDE.md v6.0 standing rule: deploy to /opt/TITAN via SSH only. The v6.1.0 BETA series HAS been pushed to GitHub + npm @beta (Tony approved). The v6.1.0 STABLE release still requires explicit Tony approval before tagging.
standing_rules.no_self_calls_at_runtime: TITAN runtime never calls Claude Code, the `claude` CLI, or any other coding agent CLI from inside its own loop. Local dev notes in ~/.claude/ are fine; runtime adapters are not.
standing_rules.explain_why: When announcing fixes/decisions: WHAT changed, WHY this approach, TRADE-OFF accepted, FOLLOW-UP queued. Standard format for handoff messages.
standing_rules.quality_over_speed: Tony's exact phrasing: 'Never skimp on quality. Always use the best approach, not shortcuts.' Solo-mode (no second pair of eyes): run the FULL test sweep on touched areas, re-read the diff before commit, smoke-probe on Titan PC after deploy.
standing_rules.no_force_push_to_main: Never force-push main. Never skip hooks (--no-verify) without explicit Tony approval.
standing_rules.verify_before_claim: Every tool call that asserts 'I did X' must produce a checkable artifact, and the runtime reads that artifact back before reporting completion. Pattern from awesome-agent-harness — see src/agent/verification.ts for the in-tree implementation.

modules_modified_this_sprint.summary: Verify-after-write primitives: verifyFileWrite (readback + byte-count + head-sample), verifyImageDownload (magic-byte sniff for PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP/AVIF, text-sniff for SVG), bounded ring buffer of recent verification events, subscribeVerification fan-out for SSE, verificationEventsSince + consecutiveTrailingFailures for the driver loop's escalation counter.

write_file / append_file / edit_file each call verifyFileWrite after writing and append the result to the return string ('[verify: …]' or '[⚠ verify FAIL: …]'). Failed verifications also push to the ring buffer.
modules_modified_this_sprint.audit_note: Three writeFileSync sites (write, edit-exact, edit-fuzzy). All three wired. Append uses pre-size capture to compute expected post-size. Path guard restricts writes to home and /tmp.

modules_modified_this_sprint.summary: After download, magic-byte sniff via verifyImageDownload BEFORE the registry push. Mismatch returns { ok: false, error: 'magic header MISMATCH …' } instead of silently embedding HTML error pages as JPEGs.
Added consecutiveAssertionFailures?: number to DriverSubtaskState. Pair with consecutiveIdenticalErrors and consecutiveNeedsInfoCount for three-pronged stuck-loop detection.

Spawn-completion branch (status==='done') walks the verification ring for events since pendingSpawn.attemptedAt. failed events with no offsetting passes → increment counter. Counter ≥ 3 → force-fail the subtask with a verify_fail message and skip to delegating.
modules_modified_this_sprint.audit_note: Threshold logic + ring scan window are the delicate piece. The defensive try/catch around the assertion counter means failures here never gate the happy path. Worth a paranoid read.

modules_modified_this_sprint.summary: New SSE endpoint GET /api/verification/stream. On connect: writes a 'snapshot' event with the last 32 ring entries, then subscribes via subscribeVerification for live fan-out. 15s heartbeat to prevent proxy reaping. Cleanup on disconnect/error.
modules_modified_this_sprint.audit_note: Auth: protected by the same token middleware as other /api/* routes. No per-user filtering — verification events are workspace-global.

modules_modified_this_sprint.summary: Deterministic LLM stub provider for CI eval. Pattern-matches the agent loop's prompt shapes: chat echo, safety refusal (rm -rf / delete everything), structured JSON envelope (spawn output), widget gate (Mission Canvas), tool calls (web_search / write_file / list_dir / read_file / web_fetch / download_image), tool-result acknowledgement. shouldUseStubProvider() gates activation on CI=true+no key OR TITAN_STUB_PROVIDER=1.
modules_modified_this_sprint.audit_note: Pattern recognizers are the public contract with the agent loop. When the agent loop's prompt shapes change, this file must change too. Tracked dependency.

modules_modified_this_sprint.summary: initProviders gated: providers.set('stub', new StubProvider()) only fires when shouldUseStubProvider() returns true. Prevents the failover walker from silently landing on the stub in production.
modules_modified_this_sprint.audit_note: If a future refactor lifts this gate, real-LLM outages would silently route to the stub and look like success in prod. The gate is load-bearing.

modules_modified_this_sprint.summary: pickDefaultModel() inserts a stub branch between the user-config-explicit check and the cloud-key checks. Returns stub/echo + reasoning model stub/json when shouldUseStubProvider() is true.
Added TITAN_STUB_PROVIDER=1 to the env block. Removed a duplicated 'Boot TITAN gateway' step. Eval suites should now actually run on every PR.

Per-spawn JSONL trajectory recorder. start / round / tool_call / tool_result / note / finish event API. Files at ~/.titan/trajectories/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<spawnId>.jsonl. Reader API: loadTrajectory(spawnId), listTrajectories({since,limit,goalId}). Tool args capped at 2 KB, results at 4 KB. Opt-out via TITAN_TRAJECTORY_RECORD=0.

Trajectory wire-in at 3 exit points: success return (done/failed), catch (failed with err), finally (aborted safety net). trajectoryHandle is nulled after each finish so the finally safety net only fires if neither happy nor error path closed it.
modules_modified_this_sprint.audit_note: Three exit points. Defensive `if (trajectoryHandle)` guards prevent double-finish. Worth a paranoid read.

Build + deploy workflow on Mac: `npm run build` (tsup → dist/) + `npm run build:ui` (vite → ui/dist/). Then `ssh titan 'sudo systemctl restart titan 2>/dev/null || pm2 restart titan 2>/dev/null || true'`. Verify with curl http://192.168.1.11:48420/api/health — HTTP 401 = service is up (auth required, expected).
Tests: `npx vitest run <files>` for scoped sweeps. `npm test` for the full suite (slow, run before stable releases).
